title: Grace period fallback artboards for onboarding quickstart
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact set of onboarding quickstart artboards and doc visuals that teach developers how to react to transient inference errors (rate limit soft-throttles, short timeouts, retry windows) using a ‘grace period’ mental model. Deliverables: artboards for console, SDK quickstart docs, and small animated microinteractions that suggest next steps (retry/backoff, switch model, preview cached output). Focus on low cognitive load, machine-parseable copy for docs PRs, and clear handoff tokens for engineering.
design_notes: Primary concept: show a three-state flow per error class: 1) Gentle: brief banner + countdown (grace period) + suggested automatic retry; 2) Actionable: persistent inline hint with single-click 'Retry with backoff' and small code snippet; 3) Recovery: successful cached/partial response preview with link to diagnostics. Visuals must include: compact console banner (single-line + small timer), modal microcopy for mobile, and a CLI/snippet panel for docs. Prefer neutral palette with amber accent for soft-throttle and red only for hard failures. Provide SVG/PNG exports and a 300–600ms Lottie for retry pulse. Include explicit token-cost hint copy and link to 'how batching affects limits' doc. Localize copy placeholders for en/fr/es.
acceptance_criteria: Three annotated artboards (console, mobile, docs snippet) delivered in Figma with handoff tags and export-ready assets
Microcopy variants A/B (compact developer, verbose educator) included and marked for doc-team pick
Animated retry microinteraction exported as Lottie and a fallback GIF for docs
Dev-ready overlay screenshots and a sample docs PR text block (JS/cURL) included in attachments
Design tokens and color contrast checks documented in the Figma spec
